chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed from Fadala ibn Ayoub from Al-'Ala' from a man from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, the lowest of what can be hoped for with the Hajj which is not Accepted from him, is that he (the pilgrim) would have Protection regarding his family and his wealth. He (the narrator) said, I said, By which thing would he have Protection regarding them? He (peace be upon him) said: Nothing (bad) would happen regarding them except for what has already happened while he was staying with them.
Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umeyr from Jundub from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The Hajj is a Jihad of the weak ones. Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) placed his hand upon his own chest and said: We are the weak ones, and we are the weak ones.
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum reward for a pilgrim whose Hajj is not accepted?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the comprehensive mercy of God, where even a 'defective' Hajj yields the tangible benefit of preserving the pilgrim's household and wealth, a concept known as *hifz al-ahl wa al-mal*. The second part elucidates the theological status of the Ahl al-Bayt as the 'weak' (*al-du'afa*) not due to lack of power, but due to their absolute reliance (*tawakkul*) on God, distinguishing their spiritual humility from worldly weakness.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Al A’ala, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The lowest of what can be hoped for with the Hajj which is not Accepted from him, is that he (the pilgrim) would have Protection regarding his family and his wealth’. He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘By which thing would he have Protection regarding them?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Nothing (bad) would happen regarding them except for what has already happened while he was staying with them’.

Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jundub, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The Hajj is a Jihad of the weak ones’. Then Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> placed his<sup>asws</sup> hand upon his<sup>asws</sup> own chest and said: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> are the weak ones, and we<sup>asws</sup> are the weak ones’.
en.sarwar: 27. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-‘Ala’ from a man who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the least with which a pilgrim, whose Hajj is not accepted, returns is safety of his family and property at home.” I (the narrator) then asked, ‘What kind of thing is this safety?’ He (the Imam) replied, ’Nothing will happen to them except things that may happen during his presence in his family and belongings.’”
